clue.text: Players dropped soprano and went with tenor instrument

indicators.note: dropped says the players' team loses one of its members here, the voice part

parts.note: a squad is a team of players
went means ran

explanation.surface: A choir manager reshuffles the singers, losing the soprano and bringing in a tenor.
explanation.walkthrough: The musical surface hides a navigational instrument rather than a musical one.
explanation.definitionFit: A quadrant is an old navigational and astronomical instrument for measuring angles.

clue.text: Fanaticism upset Zionist leader and those right-of-centre in Israel

indicators.note: the leader of a word is its first letter
upset says the gathered letters are knocked over into a new order
the letters standing to the right of the middle of the word Israel, its second half

explanation.surface: Political commentary on an overturned Zionist leader and the Israeli right.
explanation.walkthrough: 'those right-of-centre in Israel' gives AEL, the back half of ISRAEL, which 'upset' rearranges after Z.
explanation.definitionFit: Zeal is fervent, often excessive enthusiasm, a near synonym of fanatical devotion.

clue.text: Legal clause waives argument in favour of faculty

indicators.note: waives means gives up, so the clause loses these letters

parts.note: a provision is a clause in a legal document
a pro is an argument for something

explanation.surface: A contract clause sets aside a supporting argument in favour of a university faculty.
explanation.walkthrough: 'faculty' reads as a university department but means one of the senses.
explanation.definitionFit: Sight is one of the bodily faculties, so vision is a faculty in the sense of a natural power.

clue.text: Intricate pattern young woman said matches everything but the walls

indicators.note: said signals that the word for a young woman is taken by how it is spoken

parts.note: filly is informal for a lively young woman

indicators.note: the walls of a word are its outer letters, and everything except them is kept

parts.note: matches as a verb means agrees

explanation.surface: Someone decorating notes a girl said the pattern goes with everything except the walls.
explanation.walkthrough: AGREES ('matches') loses its walls, A and S, to leave GREE.
explanation.definitionFit: Filigree is delicate ornamental openwork, typically of fine metal wire, forming an intricate design.

clue.text: Don't take so much notice anyway

definitions.meaning: to pay less attention, split as regard plus less
in any case, without heeding circumstances

explanation.surface: Advice to pay less attention to something, whatever happens.
explanation.walkthrough: The first reading splits the word in two: give less regard.
explanation.definitionFit: Used as an adverb it means in spite of everything, which is what anyway means.

clue.text: People dropping ecstasy at every opportunity in Fabric

indicators.note: dropping means the word people lets go of these letters
every time the letter turns up it goes, so it is removed twice

parts.note: E is the abbreviation for the drug ecstasy

explanation.surface: Clubbers at a London nightclub called Fabric pop pills whenever they can.
explanation.walkthrough: Fabric is a well-known London nightclub, which suits the drug surface. PEOPLE loses both its Es to give POPL.
explanation.definitionFit: Poplin is a plain-woven cotton cloth used for shirts, so it is a kind of fabric.

clue.text: Unveil reforms inspired by case of Japanese youth

indicators.note: inspired by means breathed in by, so one piece goes inside the other
the case of a word is its outer letters
reforms means remakes, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A Japanese youth movement is unveiling reforms.
explanation.walkthrough: 'inspired by' means breathed in, so the case of 'Japanese' holds the rearranged letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A juvenile is a young person, a synonym for a youth.

clue.text: What time will do when you've fallen asleep

indicators.note: fallen suggests the letters have tumbled into a new order

explanation.surface: Time passes unnoticed while you sleep.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fallen' rearranges ASLEEP. The surface is literally true: the hours slip by while you are asleep.
explanation.definitionFit: Time is said to elapse when it passes, so passing is what time does.

clue.text: Reserve theatre seats for chilling performer

parts.note: ice means coldness of manner, reserve
a box is a private compartment of seats in a theatre

explanation.surface: Booking theatre seats to see a chilling performer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'chilling performer' looks like a scary actor but is something that chills, a fridge.
explanation.definitionFit: An icebox is a refrigerator, something whose job is to keep things cold.

clue.text: Projected vain image

indicators.note: projected as a voice is thrown out to be heard, so a word is taken by its sound

parts.note: vain as in futile means idle

explanation.surface: A conceited picture thrown onto a screen.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Projected' suggests a screen image, but signals a word spoken: idle sounds like the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: An idol is an image worshipped as a god, a graven image.

clue.text: It's possible gifted writer's hostile to going in the van

indicators.note: the van is the front, so these pieces lead the way before the next

parts.note: the writer is, I am, shortened to I'm
agin is dialect for against, hostile to
able means gifted

explanation.surface: A talented author is apparently opposed to riding in the van.
explanation.walkthrough: 'writer's hostile to' reads as one phrase, I'M AGIN, which goes at the front ('in the van', the vanguard) of ABLE.
explanation.definitionFit: Something imaginable can be conceived of, so it is possible.

clue.text: Unable to conceive of lawyers' split being reduced

parts.note: the Bar is the collective body of barristers

indicators.note: reduced means cut short, so the word loses its last letter

parts.note: a rent is a split or tear

explanation.surface: Barristers divided over a cost-cutting proposal they cannot imagine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'conceive of' reads as imagine, but the definition means infertile; RENT ('split') loses its T.
explanation.definitionFit: A barren woman or animal is infertile, incapable of producing offspring.

clue.text: Got back at later date after arranging where I will live?

indicators.note: the letter is given a place to live inside the arranged letters
after arranging means once the letters have been rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone settling a move to a new home at a later date.
explanation.walkthrough: 'after arranging' rearranges LATER DATE, and I settles inside ('where I will live').
explanation.definitionFit: To retaliate is to strike back in return for an injury, to get back at someone.

clue.text: Walking mud over grass verges

indicators.note: verges are edges, so these letters form the edges around the other piece

parts.note: to grass is to inform, to sing

indicators.note: over says the word mud is turned over, read backwards

parts.note: mud is dirt

explanation.surface: Someone tramping mud across roadside grass verges.
explanation.walkthrough: 'grass verges' reads as roadside lawn, but 'grass' means inform and 'verges' makes it the edges round the reversed mud.
explanation.definitionFit: Striding is walking with long steps, a vigorous kind of walking.

clue.text: Resistance figure's gained importance

indicators.note: has gained means takes on board, so the letter goes inside

parts.note: a statue is a carved figure
R is the symbol for electrical resistance

explanation.surface: A wartime Resistance figure has become important.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Resistance figure' looks like a partisan hero, but splits into R and a statue.
explanation.definitionFit: Stature means standing or reputation, how much importance someone has.

clue.text: Hits lowlife controlling vice ring!

indicators.note: controlling means holding in, so one piece surrounds the other

parts.note: a runt is a contemptible little person
a sin is a vice
O is a ring, by its shape

explanation.surface: A criminal boss running a vice ring is exposed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'vice ring' reads as an organised crime network, but splits into SIN and O.
explanation.definitionFit: To run into something is to collide with it, to hit it.

clue.text: Something on which one can play back some offbeat selections

definitions.text: Something on which one can play

indicators.note: back says the hidden letters are read backwards
some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: An invitation to play back a few unusual tracks.
explanation.definitionFit: A celesta is a keyboard instrument with metal bars, so a musician can play on it.

clue.text: Article about small period instrument

parts.note: the is the definite article
re means about, concerning
a minute, abbreviated min, is a small period of time

explanation.surface: A short piece about a little period instrument, as in early music.
explanation.walkthrough: 'period instrument' suggests early music, but 'small period' is the minute.
explanation.definitionFit: A theremin is an electronic musical instrument played without being touched.

clue.text: Saw is a perceptive gift that is returned in the end

parts.note: ESP, extrasensory perception, is a gift of perception

indicators.note: returned means sent back, so the letters are read in reverse

parts.note: i.e. abbreviates id est, that is

indicators.note: the letter in the final place of the word end

explanation.surface: Seeing is said to be a gift of perception, given back eventually.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Saw' is the past of see, not a tool; D is the last letter of 'end'.
explanation.definitionFit: To espy is to catch sight of, so espied is a past-tense synonym for saw.

clue.text: Lads went dancing in Slough and similar places

indicators.note: dancing means jigging about, so the letters move into a new order

explanation.surface: Young men went out dancing in Slough, a town west of London.
explanation.walkthrough: Slough is an English town, but here the word is a swamp or bog.
explanation.definitionFit: A slough is a muddy marsh, and marshes and bogs are wetlands.

clue.text: Rambling diatribe in support of the queen

indicators.note: in a down answer the piece below supports the one above

parts.note: ER, Elizabeth Regina, is the Queen
a rant is a diatribe

explanation.surface: A long-winded tirade in defence of the monarch.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue, 'in support of' puts RANT below ER.
explanation.definitionFit: Errant means wandering or roving, as rambling does.

clue.text: US President will broadcast a great deal for Americans

indicators.note: broadcast means spoken on air, so the phrase is taken by its sound

parts.note: the president Bush plus will shortened, as in Bush'll

explanation.surface: An American president will announce something big on the airwaves.
explanation.walkthrough: 'US President will' contracts to Bush'll, which is said like the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: In American informal use, bushels means a large amount, a great deal.

clue.text: Youthful mistake covers up cry for attention

indicators.note: covers means wraps round, so one piece surrounds the other

parts.note: bish is British slang for a blunder

indicators.note: up in a down answer says the letters read from the bottom upwards

parts.note: yo is a shout to get attention

explanation.surface: A slip hides a call for attention.
explanation.walkthrough: Bish is British slang for a mistake; 'up' reverses the cry in this down answer, and 'covers' wraps the mistake round it.
explanation.definitionFit: Boyish means like a boy, suggesting youth.

clue.text: Byzantine art I've seen in Istanbul perhaps displays originality

indicators.note: seen in means appearing inside, so one piece sits within the other

parts.note: Istanbul is an example of a city

indicators.note: Byzantine means intricate and convoluted, so the letters are tangled

explanation.surface: Byzantine art on display in Istanbul shows great originality.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Byzantine' fits Istanbul (once Byzantium) but signals the anagram of ART I'VE, which is 'seen in' the city.
explanation.definitionFit: Creativity is inventiveness, the ability to produce original work.

clue.text: European capital exuded an unpleasant smell

indicators.note: the capital letter, the first, is given off and lost

parts.note: a Greek is a European

explanation.surface: A European city gave off a bad smell.
explanation.walkthrough: 'European capital' suggests a city, but it is GREEK losing its capital letter G.
explanation.definitionFit: A reek is a strong, foul odour, a stench.

clue.text: Depend on contents of reference library? Quite the opposite!

indicators.note: contents would normally mean the inside letters of the words
the reverse of contents, so take the outside letters of each word instead

explanation.surface: A student relies on the stock of the reference library, or rather the other way round.
explanation.walkthrough: 'contents of' would mean the middles; 'Quite the opposite' flips that to the outer letters, RE and LY.
explanation.definitionFit: To rely on someone is to depend on them, trusting them for support.

clue.text: Representatives of the international community support rebellion

parts.note: the UN, United Nations, represents the international community
a rest is a support

explanation.surface: UN delegates back an uprising.
explanation.definitionFit: Unrest is disturbance and dissatisfaction amounting to revolt, close to rebellion.

clue.text: Deny Conservative leader in Daily Mail is wrong

indicators.note: in places the leading letter inside the rearranged letters

parts.note: D is short for daily

indicators.note: wrong means in error, so the letters are jumbled
the leader of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: A politician denies that the Tory leader in the Daily Mail is mistaken.
explanation.walkthrough: The Daily Mail is a British tabloid; 'wrong' gives DISLAIM, with the Conservative leader placed 'in' it.
explanation.definitionFit: To disclaim is to refuse to acknowledge or to deny responsibility for something.
